instructions: Drain and rinse the 2 cans of black beans. Spread them on a clean towel or a few paper towels and pat them as dry as you can. Wet beans make burgers that fall apart.
Grate half the onion on the big holes of a box grater. Mince the 2 garlic cloves. Take 1 chipotle pepper out of the can and chop it fine.

Put the beans in a big bowl with the grated onion, garlic, chopped chipotle, 2 tbsp of the adobo sauce from the can, 1 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp balsamic vinegar, the 1 tsp cumin, 1/2 tsp salt and 1/2 tsp pepper.
Mash it all with a potato masher or a fork until it sticks together but you can still see some whole beans.
Crack in the egg and fold it through with a spatula. Fold in the 1 cup panko until there are no dry crumbs left.

Shape the mixture into 4 patties about 3/4 inch thick. They should hold their shape and feel a little damp. If they're too soft to pick up, mash the mixture a bit more, or chill the patties for 20 minutes.
Meanwhile, wash a few lettuce leaves, slice the tomato and slice the avocado.

Heat a large cast iron or nonstick skillet over medium and add 2 tbsp olive oil. When it shimmers, lay in the patties and cook them for 5 to 6 minutes without moving them, until the underside is dark brown and crisp.

Flip them carefully with a wide spatula and cook the other side for 5 to 6 minutes, until it's browned too and the middle feels firm when you press it. Turn the heat down a little if they're darkening too fast.
While the second side cooks, toast the 4 buns cut side down in a dry pan or under the broiler for a minute or two, until golden.
Taste a corner of one patty. If it's flat, sprinkle a pinch more salt over the hot burgers.
Serve on the toasted buns with the lettuce, tomato, avocado and ketchup. Put the rest of the chipotles on the table for anyone who wants more heat.
method_notes: Both read versions mash canned black beans with garlic, an egg and panko, leaving some beans whole, and cook the patties in an oiled skillet over medium about 5 minutes a side until browned. Love and Lemons seasons them with chipotle, adobo, tamari, balsamic and cumin and chills the patties for 20 minutes if the mixture is too wet; Kristine's Kitchen pats the beans dry first, adds red pepper, green onion, ketchup and smoked paprika, and says the patties can also bake at 375°F. This follows Love and Lemons' mix (its 6 patties made into 4 larger ones) with Kristine's step of drying the beans, uses one chipotle so the patties stay mild, and puts the rest of the can on the table.
